culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Ask locally. Visit Faroe Islands: stay on marked old village paths. There is no right to roam through private outfield or sheep land, so close gates and don't disturb sheep or birds. Some hikes charge a mandatory fee or need a guide (for example Kallur, Trælanípa and Drangarnir).

items.text: The Faroe Islands are a self-governing part of the Kingdom of Denmark. Criminal law is Danish, so Danish drug law applies. The Faroes set some rules themselves, notably alcohol retail, which goes through the state alcohol shops (Rúsdrekkasøla Landsins). Penalties are not yet read.

layers.process: Mandatory hiking fees by site: Kallur lighthouse and Trøllanes (Kalsoy) DKK 200 adult, DKK 100 ages 13 to 17, free under 13, no guide included; Trælanípa and Bøsdalafossur DKK 450 adult with guide and brochure, or DKK 200 without a guide; Villingardalsfjall DKK 200 per person, paid into the mailbox at the trail gate; Nólsoy DKK 100 for commercial trips only; Mykines DKK 500 (DKK 400 booked online) from 1 May to 31 August plus the ferry, people over 15, with a mandatory guide. The page says a new Faroese sustainable tourism law will affect these fees and that details may change, so check before going. DKK amounts are not converted to A$ here (no dated rate fetched).

money-and-cost.currency: Danish krone (DKK) coins and notes, and Faroese krona banknotes issued by Danmarks Nationalbank
money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: Notes and peg: Danmarks Nationalbank prints the Faroese banknotes, in Faroese with Faroese designs. They exchange 1:1 with Danish banknotes, which is a fixed rate with the Danish krone, and coins are the same as in Denmark. Faroese notes aren't accepted as payment in Denmark but can be exchanged at banks there. The Nationalbank says older Faroese notes are still legal tender and are being withdrawn over time. Cash declaration: TAKS (Faroese Customs) requires anyone entering or leaving with 10,000 euros or more (about DKK 75,000) to declare it, under section 29 of the Faroese Customs Act; bearer bonds and money orders count too. 10,000 euros is about A$15,891 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026 (A$1 = EUR 0.6293). Forms are at Vagar airport and the Torshavn ferry terminal. Not declaring can bring a fine of 25% of the amount above 10,000 euros (minimum DKK 5,000), and customs can keep all the cash if it is suspected to be linked to crime.
money-and-cost.rate_and_date: A$1 = 0.6293 EUR (Reserve Bank of Australia, 30 October 2026); DKK 75,000 is TAKS's own approximation of 10,000 euros
